(3) result-interpreter: the interpreter agent passes solver logs, tables and plots to the LLM, which generates the human-readable explanation and what-if answer (Section 3.1.1; Figs. 5-6; Section 1: 'the output then passes through the LLM for producing the answer in human language'). Not direct-optimizer (solutions are produced by Gurobi, not proposed/iteratively improved by the LLM) and not heuristic-designer (no algorithm/heuristic design). The safeguard agent scrutinizes generated code and initiates self-debugging or error messages (Section 3.1.1; Fig. 6 'Safeguard Alert: sensitive information'), but this is code validity/safety checking (and it is not clearly LLM-based), which the schema explicitly excludes from verifier; no LLM issuance of feasibility/plausibility verdicts on models or solutions is described, so verifier is not selected.

title: LLM-Guided Transportation Hub Capacity Planning with Textual Business Inputs
or_reasoning_0.10.5: The LLM agent itself proposes and iteratively improves the first-stage solutions: it receives textual business context plus routing feedback and, via chain-of-thought reasoning over a Business Context Decision Table, proposes/modifies capacity levels {l_h} for all hubs, then refines the next candidate from updated feedback (§3 Methodology; Algorithm 1 lines 4, 14-15 'Propose refined solution l_{k+1} from T'; Figure 1). This is an OPRO-style generate-improve loop with the optimization model acting as a fixed evaluation oracle: the two-stage stochastic program is pre-existing and unchanged by the LLM ('the optimization model serves as a routing evaluation only', §3), and the context-modified 'true model' is hidden and used only for post-hoc evaluation (§4.1), so the LLM is not a formulator. The keep/discard decision (Algorithm 1 lines 9-13; §3 'Iterative Refinement Loop') is an accept/reject verdict, but it is critique inside the LLM's own generate-improve loop, so per schema it belongs to direct-optimizer rather than verifier. The LLM does not call the solver as a tool nor write solver-invoking code; the framework's fixed loop evaluates each proposal (Algorithm 1 line 7), so solver-orchestrator does not apply. No heuristic design, result interpretation, or external verification of others' solutions is present.
